detail: # GitHub profile README taste, 2025–2026

**For rewriting [github.com/iamrishab](https://github.com/iamrishab)** (special repo `iamrishab/iamrishab`). This is research only. No README draft.

**Verdict:** In 2026 the profiles that still look senior are **prose-first and evidence-first**. They answer three questions in about 15 seconds: what you ship, at what level, and where to go next. Decoration that was fashionable in 2020–2022 (GIF heroes, `for-the-badge` walls, visitor counters, streak cards, trophy boards, “Ask me about…”) now reads as junior template residue. The strongest AI/ML people often have **no profile README at all**. If you keep one, it should look closer to a short founder memo than a MySpace page.

The current `iamrishab` README is a complete specimen of the style to retire: neural GIF, emoji H2s, centered “Ask me about,” ~40 Shields badges including VS Code/PyCharm, a StackOverflow widget, streak + languages + activity-graph cards, unverified cloud certs as trophies, and a Komarev hit counter.

---

## How to read the sources

A lot of “best GitHub README 2026” posts are **SEO farms selling generators**. They recycle the same 11-second-scan copy and then recommend the widgets they monetize. I treated those as evidence of *consensus talking points*, not taste.

| Weight | Why | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| High | Official constraints, or people whose work you would actually hire | [GitHub profile README docs](https://docs.github.com/en/account-and-profile/setting-up-and-managing-your-github-profile/customizing-your-profile/managing-your-profile-readme), [GFM writing syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/getting-started-with-writing-and-formatting-on-github/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax), [theme-aware images](https://github.blog/developer-skills/github/how-to-make-your-images-in-markdown-on-github-adjust-for-dark-mode-and-light-mode/), [accessibility tips](https://github.blog/developer-skills/github/5-tips-for-making-your-github-profile-page-accessible/), [Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/2020/Jul/10/self-updating-profile-readme/), live profiles below |
| Medium | Directional, method stated | [boffti 2026 survey of 520 profile READMEs](https://github.com/boffti/github-profile-readme/blob/main/references/survey-2026.md) (39.6% prose-first; visitor counters 21.9%; dark-mode `<picture>` only 3.3%) |
| Low | Recruiter-bait / generator marketing | SlateGit, Codeboards, Quillly/DevBio, TailorCV, ReadmeDesign, GodProfile, “AI Tech Connect” |

GitHub’s own beginner guide still says you can add “text, images, animated GIFs, and emoticons as you see fit” ([Sept 2024](https://github.blog/developer-skills/github/beginners-guide-to-github-setting-up-and-securing-your-profile/)). That is onboarding copy, not senior taste. The official starter template is the ancestor of “🔭 currently working on / 💬 Ask me about.”

---

## 1. What people actually praise vs cringe

### What gets praised (hiring managers, founders, senior engineers)

**They are not grading the README as art.** HN hiring threads from 2018–2024 are consistent: if they open GitHub, they want to know whether you can build and explain software. The profile box is a frame. The proof is pinned repos, commit judgment, and project READMEs.

- **A specific one-line identity.** “AI Research Engineer working on LLMs” ([rasbt](https://github.com/rasbt)) beats “passionate full-stack developer.” Recruiter-oriented writeups all converge here: [SlateGit 11-second scan](https://slategit.com/blog/github-profile-readme-recruiter-tips-11-second-scan), [TailorCV 2026](https://thetailorcv.com/blog/github-profile-for-job-search-2026).
- **Selected work with outcomes.** Three to five projects, each with a number and a link. Not a skill inventory. Samuel Faj’s 2026 AI-portfolio piece is the adult version: problem → decision → run it → proof → limits ([samuelfaj.com](https://www.samuelfaj.com/en/blog/ai-software-engineer-portfolio-what-to-prove/)).
- **Pinned repos that match the README.** Empty or tutorial-fork pins under a “LangGraph / CrewAI / AutoGen” banner is a credibility miss. Pins are the real portfolio; the profile README is the caption.
- **An obvious next step.** Email, site, or LinkedIn. The 2026 survey found **41% of profile READMEs had no email / LinkedIn / X link**.
- **Restraint as a seniority signal.** Karpathy, Chip Huyen, Hamel Husain, Jason Liu, Sebastian Raschka: no profile README. The work is the page. That is the taste you are competing with, not Anurag Hazra clones.
- **Live content that is actually yours.** Simon Willison’s auto-updated releases / blog / TILs is still the cleanest “dynamic README” in the genre because it is a **feed of work**, not a dashboard of vanity.

### What gets cringed (often silently)

Senior readers rarely write “your README is cringe.” They bounce. The tells:

| Signal | Why it lands badly in 2026 |
|---|---|
| GIF header / neural-net animation | 2020–2021 generator look. Burns the fold. Inaccessible. Says “I decorated GitHub” not “I shipped systems.” |
| `for-the-badge` wall (Git, VS Code, Pandas…) | Lists tools a junior bootcamp also lists. Implies you need logos because you lack proof. |
| “Ask me about…” / 🔭🌱💬 template | Unfilled or lightly filled GitHub default. The #1 genre smell in the [boffti pitfalls list](https://github.com/boffti/github-profile-readme/blob/main/references/pitfalls-checklist.md). |
| Visitor counter | Hits, not people. Camo-proxied, bot-inflated. Low looks sad; high looks try-hard. Even [komarev’s own README](https://github.com/antonkomarev/github-profile-views-counter) says it is for *you*, not visitors. |
| Trophy board / streak card | Gamified activity. Easy to farm. HN has treated GitHub achievement badges as noise since the [2022 Achievements beta](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=31682718). |
| Snake / Pac-Man on the contribution graph | Cute in 2021. In 2026 it is the default “I followed a YouTube tutorial.” |
| Stats cards as the hero | Public-only, rate-limited, often broken (“Max retries exceeded”). They cannot see private production work. [Anurag Hazra’s public instance](https://github.com/anuraghazra/github-readme-stats) is a known reliability problem. |
| Unverified cert dump | For a senior, listing AWS/GCP/Azure ML certs without credential IDs or dates reads as LinkedIn padding. If they are real, one line with a link. If not, delete. |
| StackOverflow widget | 2015 portfolio energy. Irrelevant to AI hiring. |
| “Enterprise AI Solutions” / “next-gen” | LLM-brochure voice. The opposite of founder voice. |
| Agent-readable `AGENTS.md` / `llms.txt` theater on a profile | Clever once. On a personal profile it currently reads as 2026 maximalism unless you already have a public body of work those files describe. |

**Audience split you should design for**

- **Founders / staff+ engineers:** they want judgment, constraints, and one or two sharp artifacts. They discount widgets.
- **Recruiters / ATS-adjacent scanners:** they want role, stack keywords, and contact in the first screen. They will not decode a GIF.
- **You do not need two READMEs.** One short page can serve both if the first 12 lines are identity + proof + contact, and the stack is a short word list, not a logo dump.

---

## 2. Exemplary profiles (12)

Prefer these over “awesome README” galleries. Those galleries over-index on animation.

### Editorial / minimal (copy the discipline, not the jokes)

**1. Cassidy Williams — [github.com/cassidoo](https://github.com/cassidoo)** · [raw README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cassidoo/cassidoo/master/README.md) 
Opens “Hello, nerds.” No stats, no badges, no GIFs. A paragraph of voice, then a bullet list of things she made, each a real URL. This is what “personality” looks like when it is not emoji headers.

**2. Caneco — [github.com/caneco](https://github.com/caneco)** · [raw README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/caneco/caneco/master/README.md) 
Six lines. Role, employer, community, daily tools as file extensions (`.php`, `.svg`), designed artifacts with names. The old “ping me about design / Laravel” line is the only dated bit. Still the cleanest minimal card in the awesome-list set.

**3. The no-README cluster (this is the actual senior AI default)** 
[karpathy](https://github.com/karpathy) (“I like to train Deep Neural Nets on large datasets.” — sidebar only), [chiphuyen](https://github.com/chiphuyen) (“AI x stuff”), [rasbt](https://github.com/rasbt), [hamelsmu](https://github.com/hamelsmu), [jxnl](https://github.com/jxnl). 
They let pins and repos do the talking. For a founder with a thin public graph, you *should* have a README — but it should aspire to this density, not to a dashboard.

### AI / ML people who actually wrote one

**4. Maxime Labonne — [github.com/mlabonne](https://github.com/mlabonne)** · [raw README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlabonne/mlabonne/main/README.md) 
The right IA for an AI person: one sentence, then **Projects / Models / Books**, each item a named artifact with a parenthetical proof (`>80k ⭐`, “first successful open-source DPO”). Contact is a single icon row. No streak, no snake, no “ask me about LangChain.”

**5. Simon Willison — [github.com/simonw](https://github.com/simonw)** · [repo](https://github.com/simonw/simonw) · [writeup](https://simonwillison.net/2020/Jul/10/self-updating-profile-readme/) 
Still the gold standard for dynamic profiles. One sentence of current work + blog/newsletter. Then three columns: recent releases, blog, TILs, injected by Actions via HTML comment markers. No cards. The dynamism *is the work*. Updated into 2026.

**6. Peter Steinberger — [github.com/steipete](https://github.com/steipete)** · [raw README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/steipete/main/README.md) 
Use the **top**, not the whole page. Founder + agents: one-line context (ex-PSPDFKit, now OpenAI), then **Start Here** with star counts (`OpenClaw 387k+`). That “selected work with a number” pattern is correct. The rest is a 100-item catalog and should not be copied. Proof that even a strong founder over-writes.

### Technically rich, still premium

**7. Orhun Parmaksız — [github.com/orhun](https://github.com/orhun)** · [raw README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orhun/orhun/master/README.md) 
Systems person, not a frontend showcase. The move to steal: **stats as a sentence** (“joined 9 years ago… 32,230 commits… 22,885 stars across 158 personal projects”) plus a two-column project table with one-line descriptions. Custom visuals sit *after* the prose. Kill his visitor counter if you copy the rest.

**8. Lowlighter — [github.com/lowlighter](https://github.com/lowlighter)** · [metrics engine](https://github.com/lowlighter/metrics) 
The honest technically-rich profile: a short status note in his own voice, then **self-hosted SVG infographics** generated by his own Action, not a public Vercel card. If you want dynamic visuals in 2026, this is the architecture (your Action, your SVG, your theme). Do not embed the kitchen-sink default of `lowlighter/metrics` plugins.

**9. Adrij Shikhar — [github.com/adrijshikhar](https://github.com/adrijshikhar)** · [raw README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adrijshikhar/adrijshikhar/main/README.md) · [writeup](https://adrijshikhar.dev/blogs/building-an-agentic-era-profile-readme/) 
Best *human* block of any “custom SVG” profile I opened: role, one origin sentence, then bullets with real numbers (`25K+ source objects`, `60s → sub-second`, `1,889 PRs / 47 repos`). Custom widgets are theme-aware. Then he spends the rest of the page on snake, Minesweeper-via-issues, and `AGENTS.md`. Steal the first screen. Leave the arcade.

### Restrained hybrids worth stealing one idea from

**10. Stefanie Grunwald — [github.com/moertel](https://github.com/moertel)** · [raw README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moertel/moertel/master/README.md) 
Data/platform engineer. One sentence, a **muted flat-square** language/tools row (not `for-the-badge`), then role. Personality without a carnival.

**11. Anurag Hazra — [github.com/anuraghazra](https://github.com/anuraghazra)** · [raw README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anuraghazra/anuraghazra/master/README.md) 
Creator of the stats cards everyone overuses. The only line that still works: “Built github-readme-stats… **50m+ hits • 50K stars**.” Everything else is 2020 template. Lesson: one verified number beats a widget that *displays* numbers.

**12. Sindre Sorhus — [github.com/sindresorhus](https://github.com/sindresorhus)** 
Do **not** copy the Geocities parody unless you have 80k followers and are making a joke. Included because it is the rare profile that knows the genre is exhausted and comments on it. Your audience will not read irony; they will read clutter.

**Honorable mention (technique, not taste):** [veggiedefender](https://github.com/veggiedefender) (sliced-image clickable UI) and [platane](https://github.com/platane) (snake generator). Historically clever. In 2026 they are the problem.

---

## 3. Anti-patterns to kill (opinionated)

Kill these. Do not “tone them down.” Do not hide them in `<details>` “for fun.” A senior page that still contains a visitor counter is a senior who did not finish the edit.

1. **GIF / neural / capsule-render heroes.** They eat the fold, fail alt-text, and date the page to 2021. Your `assets/hello.gif` + `assets/neural.gif` go first.
2. **Centered emoji H2s** (`🚀 About Me`, `🧰 Tech Stack`). Center art, not biography. GitHub’s accessibility guidance: real headings, plain language, emoji restraint ([GitHub Blog](https://github.blog/developer-skills/github/5-tips-for-making-your-github-profile-page-accessible/)).
3. **The GitHub starter bullets.** `🔭 currently working on` / `💬 Ask me about` / `⚡ specializing in`. This is the unfilled official template with model names dropped in.
4. **Badge walls, especially `for-the-badge`.** One style, ≤8 technologies you would defend in a design review. **Git, VS Code, PyCharm, Jupyter, and “Cursor” as a skill are not skills.** Listing AWS + GCP + Azure + every datastore is a junior range-claim.
5. **Visitor counters** (`komarev.com/ghpvc`). Vanity, inaccurate (Camo), and 21.9% of the 2026 sample — common enough to look generic.
6. **Trophy boards** (`github-profile-trophy`). Decorative ranks. 7.9% incidence. Omit.
7. **Streak cards.** They reward commit theater. Yours is on `github-readme-streak-stats.herokuapp.com`, which has a long history of outages.
8. **Activity-graph / snake / Pac-Man.** Third-party Vercel graphs plus contribution-eating animations. Novelty embeds; they push proof down.
9. **StackOverflow / WakaTime / Spotify / “now playing” / random-dev-quote.** Wrong site, wrong decade, or a secret you are leaking.
10. **Unverified certification trophies.** Four cloud/NVIDIA lines with no IDs, dates, or links is worse than silence. Seniors who have the certs link Credly once or put them on LinkedIn.
11. **Public stats cards as identity.** They measure public commits. Your production ML will not show up. When the public renderer 429s, your profile shows a broken image.
12. **Fancy Unicode / mathematical-bold headings.** Screen readers spell them as gibberish. Looks “designed” in a generator preview; fails a11y.
13. **Typing SVGs** (`readme-typing-svg`). Motion text that is not selectable, not searchable, and not readable by assistive tech. 5.6% of the survey; already a cliché.
14. **Two badge styles, two card themes, `theme=dark` hardcoded.** Breaks light mode. Inconsistent chrome is how a page looks assembled from tutorials.
15. **Copy-paste leftover usernames / empty `alt` / `#` links.** Survey: 47.3% missing alt text. Your SO and some social images already fail this.
16. **`AGENTS.md` on a personal profile, glassmorphic “GodProfile” SVGs, LLM-generated bento grids.** The 2026 version of the 2021 badge wall.

If you want a single heuristic: **if a recruiter could screenshot it and it would still look like 50 other “AI engineer” profiles, it is an anti-pattern.**

---

## 4. SOTA that still looks premium in 2026

Premium here means: still looks intentional in two years, works in light and dark, does not depend on a stranger’s Vercel quota, and does not scream “README generator.”

### Custom inline SVGs (light / dark)

**What works**

- Self-host SVG in the profile repo. Relative path. Correct default branch (`master` vs `main` — 17.7% of surveyed profiles hard-code the wrong one).
- Official theme switch, April 2025 ([GitHub Blog](https://github.blog/developer-skills/github/how-to-make-your-images-in-markdown-on-github-adjust-for-dark-mode-and-light-mode/)):

```html
<picture>
 <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="assets/mark-dark.svg">
 <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="assets/mark-light.svg">
 <img alt="Short description of the graphic" src="assets/mark-light.svg">
</picture>
```

- Or one SVG with `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` in an internal `<style>`. This still works when Camo caches the file because the browser evaluates CSS locally ([DEV writeup](https://dev.to/igorcbraz/solving-darklight-themes-in-svgs-on-github-without-dom-access-bypassing-camo-155d)).
- Match Primer: light canvas `#ffffff` / `#f6f8fa`, dark `#0d1117`, text `#24292f` / `#c9d1d9`.
- Use SVG for a **small** mark, a selected-work strip, or a single architecture glyph. Height ~40–120px. Not a 480×270 neural loop.

**What breaks**

- Inline `<svg>…</svg>` in the README is sanitized. Ship a file, reference it with `<img>` / `<picture>`.
- External SVG CDNs (Simple Icons, random widget hosts) go through [Camo](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/about-anonymized-urls). Scripts, some fonts, and `foreignObject` die. Icons can flip from inline to block and wrap one-per-line.
- `#gh-dark-mode-only` URL fragments are **deprecated**. Use `<picture>`.
- Glassmorphism, animated marquees, “neural maps,” 3D globes: technically possible, taste-negative.

Dark-mode `<picture>` appeared in **only 3.3%** of the 2026 sample. Doing it correctly is a quality marker precisely because almost nobody bothers.

### Dynamic GitHub Actions content

**Still premium:** the Simon Willison pattern.

- HTML comment sentinels (`<!-- recent_releases starts -->` … `ends -->`).
- Cron + `workflow_dispatch` + on-push.
- Script writes **markdown you could have typed**: links, dates, one-line titles.
- Source of truth is *your* GraphQL / RSS / API, not `github-readme-stats`.

**Acceptable if you maintain it:** a self-hosted SVG generated in CI (Lowlighter-style, or a 40-line Python that draws three metrics you care about: e.g. “evals run this month,” “models in prod,” “posts”).

**Not premium:** public widgets that refetch on every profile view. They flake, they leak the fact that you use the same theme as 10k students, and they cannot see private work.

**Ops constraints**

- Actions on a profile repo go stale if the account is quiet; GitHub disables scheduled workflows after inactivity. Do not add keepalive hacks (ToS smell).
- If the feed can be empty, do not show “No activity tracked” (see [abhisheknaiidu’s WakaTime block](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhisheknaiidu/abhisheknaiidu/master/README.md)). Empty automation is worse than a static sentence.

### Metric-first selected work

This is the only “widget” seniors respect, and it is not a widget.

Pattern (Labonne / Orhun / Shikhar / Steinberger’s “Start Here”):

- Name of the system
- One clause of what it does
- One number with a unit (latency, users, stars only if they are real, $ only if you can stand behind it)
- Link to repo, paper, post, or product

A number without a method is worse than no number. “Reduced routing 60%” needs a denominator. Faj is right about this.

For you, stars on 2018–2019 CV/OCR repos are the wrong metric. Prefer production outcomes, even if the code is closed: latency, volume, eval score, cost, incidents, customers. Closed-source work belongs **in the profile README** because it will never appear in the contribution graph.

### Typography and spacing inside GitHub’s box

You cannot set fonts. `style` / `class` / `id` are stripped ([github/markup sanitizer](https://github.com/github/markup)). Design is hierarchy + whitespace.

- **Left-align prose.** Center only a short mark or a compact link row.
- **One real heading level at a time.** `#` once or not at all (the profile already shows your name). Then `##` sections. Do not skip levels.
- **Blank line = paragraph.** In `.md` files a single newline is a space; use two spaces, `\`, or `<br>` for a hard break ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/getting-started-with-writing-and-formatting-on-github/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax)).
- **`---` sparingly** as a section break. Three in a row looks like a template.
- **Lists over centered `<p>` stacks.** Your current About is four centered paragraphs. That is why it feels like a flyer.
- **Tables: 2–3 columns, short cells.** Good for selected work. Bad as a layout grid.
- **`<details><summary>`** for optional proof (talks, full stack, certs). Officially supported ([collapsed sections](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/working-with-advanced-formatting/organizing-information-with-collapsed-sections)). Only 9% of profiles use it; it is the correct place for anything after the fold.
- **Alerts** (`> [!NOTE]`) exist. Use at most one, or none. They look like docs, not a bio.
- **Math** (`$...$`, ` ```math `) works if you ever need a loss/eval expression. Do not use it as decoration.
- **Mermaid** works in Markdown files ([diagrams docs](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/working-with-advanced-formatting/creating-diagrams)). A 6-node agent diagram can earn its place. A 20-node spaghetti chart will not render well on mobile.

### What GitHub Markdown actually supports — and what breaks on mobile

**Works in profile READMEs**

- GFM: headings, lists, tables, images, footnotes, task lists (read-only), emoji shortcodes, autolinks
- HTML subset: `a`, `img`, `picture`/`source`, `div`/`p` with `align`, `br`, `details`/`summary`, `table` + `colspan`/`rowspan`, `sup`/`sub`/`kbd`
- Attributes that survive: `href`, `src`, `alt`, `title`, `width`, `height`, `align`, `target`
- Safe URLs: `http(s)`, `mailto`, relative

**Stripped / blocked**

- `script`, `style`, `iframe`, `form`, `input`, `textarea` (GFM tagfilter)
- Inline CSS, `class`, `id`
- Custom fonts, CSS grid, flexbox
- Inline SVG DOM (use an image file)

**Camo**

- Every external image is rewritten through `camo.githubusercontent.com`. No cookies, no reliable unique visitors, aggressive cache. This is why hit counters lie and why random badge CDNs flake.

**Mobile / GitHub app**

- The README sits **above** pins. A 270px GIF + badge wall means a phone user never sees work.
- Wide default stats cards (~495px) and 2-column “layout tables” horizontal-scroll.
- `for-the-badge` wraps into a ragged stack; `flat-square` is merely ugly, not broken.
- `align="right"` images collide with text under ~400px.
- GIFs autoplay and are expensive on cellular.
- `prefers-color-scheme` follows the **OS / GitHub theme**, which is what you want.
- Mermaid and wide tables are the first things to overflow. Preview in a 390px window before you ship.
- Footnotes work; they dump at the bottom, which on a profile is after a long scroll — fine for one citation, bad as a habit.

## 5. Information architecture for a senior AI founder

**Goal:** frame 8–9 years of production ML, agents, RAG, CV, and a company — without looking like you are job-hunting with a bootcamp template.

Recommended order. Keep the rendered first screen under ~25 lines.

| # | Section | What it contains | What it is not |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Identity** | Name optional (sidebar has it). One sentence: role × domain × altitude. Founder title only if the company is nameable. | “Senior AI Engineer \| GenAI \| Agentic \| RAG \| CV \| MLOps” |
| 2 | **Frame** | 3–5 sentences. Years, where you have shipped (industry, not “enterprise”), what “production” means (latency, evals, humans-in-the-loop, cost). One human texture max. | Origin story, “passionate about,” tool laundry list |
| 3 | **Selected work** | 3–5 items. Closed-source allowed. Metric + link or “private / ask.” This is the page. | 88-repo inventory, 2018 course projects unless one is still the best public artifact |
| 4 | **Now** | Current company/product and 1–3 concrete threads. Dated in your head; rewrite quarterly. | “Currently working on Multi-Agent AI Systems” |
| 5 | **Writing / talks** | 0–3 links if they exist. Or omit. | Medium-rss embed |
| 6 | **Contact** | Plain email + LinkedIn + site. One primary CTA. | Four social badge colors + follower count |
| 7 | **Optional `<details>`** | Tight stack as **words** (PyTorch, the actual serving path, the actual vector store). Verified certs with links. Older CV/OCR work. | Open-by-default widget pile |

**Omit entirely**

Visitor counter, streak, trophies, snake, SO, activity graph, “ask me about,” fun facts, currently learning, Spotify, WakaTime, Pronouns-as-a-section (put pronouns in the GitHub profile field if you want them), vs-code-as-a-skill, unverified multi-cloud certs, the neural GIF.

**Do not duplicate the sidebar.** Company, location, website, and bio already render on the left. The README should add *work*, not repeat “AI engineer in X.”

**Pins are part of the IA.** After the rewrite, pin 4–6 repos that match section 3. A profile README that claims agents + RAG above pins of 2018 energy-regression and a CES golf-cart demo will be read as a rewrite of the *page*, not the *career*. Either update pins or write one honest line about what is public vs private.

**Length target:** 150–400 words of prose plus a short selected-work list. Labonne is the upper bound for a clean AI page. Steinberger is the failure mode (catalog). Simon is the failure mode only if you do not actually publish.

---

## 6. Voice that does not sound like ChatGPT or LinkedIn

Ghostwrite from **facts**, then cut until it sounds like Slack to a peer.

### Ban list (current README already trips several)

**ChatGPT / brochure:** passionate, leveraging, cutting-edge, next-gen, robust, scalable (naked), seamless, ecosystem, landscape, delve, empower, unlock, transformative, “I’m excited to,” “feel free to reach out,” “I specialize in X, Y, and Z,” triadic adjective stacks, em-dash addiction.

**LinkedIn-bro:** thought leader, results-driven, proven track record, synergy, “open to connecting,” “I help companies accelerate their AI journey,” ninja/guru/rockstar, “Enterprise AI Solutions.”

**GitHub-template:** Ask me about, fun fact, currently learning, “building with Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama.”

### Principles

1. **Interview first, draft second.** List 8–12 facts you can defend (systems, numbers, years, company names, failed approaches). The README may only use those facts. This is the only reliable way to stop a model from inventing seniority.
2. **Nouns that exist in the world.** Products, papers, pipelines, customers, hardware. Not “agentic frameworks.”
3. **Verbs of shipping.** Built, replaced, cut, evaluated, onboarded, killed. Not specializing / focusing / passionate about.
4. **One idea per sentence.** If you would not say it aloud, cut it. Read the page out loud. If you wince, rewrite.
5. **Under-claim.** Seniors leave air. “I work on production RAG” is weaker than “We serve X with a retriever that we eval weekly on Y.” The second is still calm.
6. **Numbers need a method.** “p95 1.2s on the internal eval set, n=…” or don’t use the number.
7. **One texture, not a Fun Facts section.** Cassidy’s “jokes and musicals” works because the rest is work. A random “I love coffee” line on an otherwise generic AI page is worse.
8. **First person, short.** “I” is fine. “We” is fine for the company. “One” / “the author” is not.
9. **Do not write the bio the model wants to write.** If a sentence could sit on 500 Hugging Face profiles, it is wrong. “Building with Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama” is that sentence.
10. **Final pass: delete the first paragraph.** People bury the actual claim under a throat-clear. Start at the sentence you were afraid was too blunt.

### Translation from the current page (illustrative, not a draft)

| Now | Why it fails | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| “I’m currently working on Multi-Agent AI Systems, LLM Orchestration, and Agentic Frameworks.” | Capitalized product-category soup | Name the system and the job it does |
| “Building with Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama… for next-gen AI applications.” | Model-name dropping + “next-gen” | Models are implementation details unless you *trained* or *eval’d* them |
| “Ask me about AI Agent Architectures, LLM Fine-tuning, and Enterprise AI Solutions” | Template + brochure | Delete the section. If someone should ask you something, your selected work will prompt it |
| Four cloud cert trophies | Unverified, generic | One linked cred or nothing |
| 40 badges | Range-claim | Eight words you would staff a project with |

Voice models to internalize: Karpathy’s sidebar sentence; Labonne’s project lines; Willison’s “Currently working on Datasette, LLM and associated projects”; Orhun’s commit-count paragraph. None of them sound generated because they attach to **named artifacts**.

---

## Implications for `iamrishab` (without writing it)

The rewrite is not a restyle. It is a **genre change**: from 2021 generator profile to 2026 founder memo.

What the current file is doing wrong, in order of damage:

1. The fold is two GIFs.
2. The About block is the official emoji template filled with 2024–2026 buzzwords.
3. There is **zero selected work** on a profile whose public repos are mostly 2018–2019 CV/OCR — so the README is papering over a public/private split instead of explaining it.
4. The badge wall claims a full MLOps + three-cloud + every database surface.
5. Widgets (SO, streak, top langs, activity graph, views) occupy more vertical space than any claim about production systems.
6. Certifications are presented as a trophy case.

What a senior visitor should see instead, in the first screen: who you are, what you have actually shipped (including private), what you are building now, how to reach you. Everything else is optional and collapsed.

If public GitHub is not where the real work lives, **say that once** and point at the company site, a case study, or a filtered set of pins. Pretending the contribution graph plus LangChain badges is the portfolio is the thing that reads as 2021.

**Living Datum** is the system. One idea carries the whole profile: a surveyed origin that does not drift, with a loss that is still breathing. That is Immovable and “feeling alive” in a single object. It is not a terminal, not a badge wall, and not a widget kit sitting on rounded cards.

GitHub’s profile column is roughly **830px on desktop** and **~360px on mobile**, with images at `max-width: 100%`. Every composition below is authored at **880 viewBox units**, stacked (not multi-column), and designed so the story still reads at **0.41×**.

---

## 1. Visual concept — Living Datum

### Intent
Founders and CTOs should feel they opened an instrument, not a generated profile. The page is a **datum**: a fixed reference you measure from. The motion is a **loss that finds a basin and stays alive there**. The personal hook and the company name become one mark instead of a slogan plus a logo.

Immovable Tech already owns CLI / `$ cat` / block-cursor on the marketing site. The profile must stay in the same family of seriousness and **not clone that terminal**. No green-on-black shell. No typing caret.

### Palette — Filament on paper / filament on carbon

Transparent ground. No painted panels. The SVG sits on GitHub’s own surface (`#ffffff` light, `#0d1117` dark). That single choice is what keeps this from looking like GPRM / github-readme-stats / capsule-render.

| Token | Light | Dark | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ink / bone | `#1C1916` | `#E8E2D6` | Hook, primary marks |
| Muted | `#6F6A63` | `#9A948A` | Labels, secondary type |
| Hairline | `#D4CFC6` | `#3F3A34` | Rules, axes, topology |
| **Filament** | `#C45C26` | `#E39B55` | The living accent — only this moves in a loop |
| Basin | filament @ 10% | filament @ 14% | Soft fill at the minimum, never a glow blob |
| Forbidden | neon cyan, matrix green, `#00FF88`, rainbow gradients, pure `#000` fills, badge-brand colors | | |

Filament is copper/ember: a healthy lamp, a thermocouple, a plotter pen. It is warm on purpose so it cannot be mistaken for “AI cyan.” The old `neural.gif` teal is retired, not evolved.

### Type
- **Display (hook only):** a real text serif with an italic — Newsreader or Source Serif 4, display optical size. The sentence is the only place serif appears. **“feeling alive.” is the only italic in the system.**
- **Instrument:** IBM Plex Mono (OFL), tracked slightly open, all-caps for three-letter beats (`SEE` / `CHOOSE` / `ACT`), sentence case for `now`.
- **Body / identity / links:** GitHub’s own markdown type. Do not SVG-wrap every heading. Real text is what search, a11y, and the profile index see.
- **Never:** Inter, Space Grotesk, JetBrains Mono, Fira Code, “Hi I’m” script, balloon lettering from `hello.gif`.

### Motion language — Plotter
Motion is a pen finishing a line, then a needle ticking at rest. Not a loader, not a greeting.

- One **draw** (stroke-dashoffset, 1.8–2.8s, ease-out, `fill="freeze"`).
- One **settle** (datum mark appears when the curve arrives).
- One **alive tick** (filament dot, 2–3 viewBox units, 10–14s, almost imperceptible).
- Easing is plotter ease-out. No bounce, no elastic, no rainbow interpolation.

### The sigil
A circle (basin) + a crosshair sitting slightly below center (the minimum) + a short descending curve entering from upper left (the loss) + one filament particle at the intersection. This is the section mark. It replaces emoji headers.

---

## 2. Exact asset list

Retire `assets/hello.gif` and `assets/neural.gif`. Do not keep them as easter eggs in the README.

**Canvas rule:** `viewBox="0 0 880 H"`. Embed as `<img width="880">` (no height). GitHub scales width; aspect holds.

**Dark/light rule:** identical geometry, token swap only. Never two different compositions. Official GitHub method: `<picture>` + `prefers-color-scheme`. Do **not** rely on `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` *inside* a single SVG — GitHub’s theme and the SVG-as-`<img>` color-scheme do not always agree.

**Type in files:** outline the hook and all display words to paths in the built files. If `now` is generated, embed a **subset** IBM Plex Mono WOFF2 (`@font-face` data URI inside the SVG). External font URLs are blocked in SVG-as-image.

| File | Size | Contains | Motion | Dark/light |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assets/dist/sigil-light.svg` `sigil-dark.svg` | **48×48** (`0 0 48 48`) | Living Datum mark only. No type. | Filament particle: 12s opacity 0.55↔1.00 and 1.5-unit vertical tick. | Token swap |
| `assets/dist/hero-light.svg` `hero-dark.svg` | **880×320** | **Stacked, not split.** Three lines of outlined serif (the hook). Sigil sits after the last word, not in a right-hand column. Full-width hairline **loss curve as a horizon under the sentence** — the basin lands under “alive.” Quiet mono tick labels on the axis (`t`, `L`) at ≥28 units so they survive mobile. No name, no “AI engineer,” no greeting. | Curve draws 2.4s once and freezes. Datum mark fades in at t=2.2s. Filament dot at the minimum ticks 12s forever. | Token swap |
| `assets/dist/act-light.svg` `act-dark.svg` | **880×88** | Three words on one polyline: `SEE · CHOOSE · ACT` (or `OBSERVE · DECIDE · ACT` if the words still read at 360px — test at 0.41×; prefer the shorter set). No boxes, no icons, no chevrons. Hairline path is the same plotter stroke family as the hero horizon. | A 5×5 filament square travels the path on a **14s** loop and **parks on ACT for ~40% of the cycle**. That pause *is* the positioning. | Token swap |
| `assets/dist/work-light.svg` `work-dark.svg` | **880×260** | **Three stacked rows**, not three columns. Each row: index `01` (muted mono) · **metric as the hero number** (serif or mono tabular, ≥56 units) · one-line domain (muted, ≥28 units). Hairline between rows. No rounded cards, no logos, no company lockups. Anatomy only — copy is filled later from real metrics. | None, or a 16s 4% opacity breath on the three numbers together. Prefer none. | Token swap |

Hairline circles, 1px strokes, labels under nodes at ≥26 units. No vendor logos, no pills, no brand hex. Optional faint filament on the `AGENTS → SERVE` hop only (the “acts” hop). | A filament tick walks the spine 16s, same park-on-the-act idea, quieter than `act`. | Token swap |

**Do not create:** `banner-*.svg`, `divider-*.svg`, `features-*.svg`, `badges/*`, `typing.svg`, `stats.svg`, `footer-wave.svg`. Those filenames are how 2021–2025 generators announce themselves.

**Size budget:** hero ≤ 80KB (paths, no full font). Others ≤ 25KB. `now` + subset mono ≤ 40KB. Camo ceiling is 5MB; that is irrelevant. The real ceiling is “feels hand-made, not a dump.”

---

## 3. Section layout on github.com/iamrishab

Left rail is GitHub’s (avatar, handle, followers). You do not fight it. The README is the right column, **left-aligned**, no `<p align="center">`, no emoji `##` headers.

**Top → bottom, as rendered:**

1. **Hero SVG** (`hero` via `<picture>`). First paint. The hook is the headline. No GIF, no “Hi,” no name lockup — the profile sidebar already has the name.
2. **8–12px gap** (a markdown blank line). Then **2–3 lines of real markdown**: who he is, Immovable Tech as a text link, the positioning sentence in words. This is indexable and selectable. The SVG must not be the only place those facts exist.
3. **Act SVG.** The visual sentence for “AI that acts, not just answers.” No second slogan badge above it.
4. **Markdown `##` in plain text** (one word, e.g. the work section title — written later). Then **Work SVG**. Each row can be wrapped in `<a href="...">` if a public case exists; otherwise the SVG is mute and links sit as one markdown line under it. Do not use a 3-column table — it collapses to unreadable on the profile’s narrow mobile column.
5. **Stack SVG.** Systems he actually ships, as a schematic. This replaces the entire for-the-badge wall.
6. **Now SVG** (Action-fed). Then **real markdown links** on their own line: mail, LinkedIn, Immovable. Do not put the only contact path inside an SVG (not selectable, not reliable for AT).
7. **Optional `<details>`** for certifications / older proof. Closed by default. No trophy row, no SO widget, no streak card, no language donut, no activity graph, no visitor counter, no follower badge.

**What is gone from the current page:** centered waving `hello.gif`, dancing `neural.gif`, five badge catalogs, StackOverflow card, streak/stats/graph trio, emoji section headers, komarev views.

**Length target:** hook + identity + act above the fold on desktop. Whole README ≈ **1.5–2 desktop viewports**. Pinned repos below the README should still be reachable. A long SVG landing page is the new generator look.

**Mobile:** one column of full-width images. Hero stays stacked (type over horizon). Work stays stacked rows. If any label dies at 360px, enlarge it or delete it — do not add a second mobile SVG.

---

## 4. Motion: tasteful vs cheap

**Tasteful (use these)**
- A line that **draws once and stops**. The brain reads it as writing, not as a loader.
- A mark that **arrives late** (datum after the curve). Sequence = craft.
- A particle that **ticks at rest** (2–3 units, ≥10s). Alive, not busy.
- A token that **travels then parks** on ACT. Motion with a point of view.
- Shared timing: hero draw 2.4s, loops 10–16s. One clock for the page.

**Cheap (ban these)**
- Typing “Hi I’m Rishab” / rotating role strings / block cursor walk. That is denvercoder1 / ScribeSVG, regardless of font.
- Rainbow stroke, gradient shimmer, glow bloom, particle field, orbiting logos.
- Bounce, elastic, spin, snake, waving hands, dancing mascots (`hello.gif` / `neural.gif` energy).
- Looping stroke-dash on a box around a “card.”
- Badge wiggle, trophy shine, visitor-count increment.
- Anything that still looks like a loading state after 3 seconds.
- More than **one** traveling token visible at a time. Hero ticks. Act travels. Stack may tick *or* be still. Not all three chasing.

**Reduced motion:** SMIL cannot see `prefers-reduced-motion`. Keep amplitudes so small that the page is still usable if the loop never stops. First frame of every SVG must be a complete, readable composition (curve already at the basin, token already on ACT, `now` line fully visible). No “empty then type on.” If you later want a hard off switch, the build can emit `*-static.svg` and a third `<source media="(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)">` — v1 should not need it if motion stays this quiet.

---

## 5. Maximal without looking like a 2021 generator

Maximal here means **fewer objects, higher finish** — not more widgets.

| Generator tell | Living Datum rule |
|---|---|
| Centered everything | Left lock. Sidebar already centers the face. |
| Rounded dark cards on the page | Transparent. Hairlines only. No `rx` chrome. |
| Banner + dividers + feature grid + footer wave | Five compositions, no divider files. |
| for-the-badge / logo salad | Topology with words. Zero vendor marks. |
| Typing intro + snake + trophies + views | None of those surfaces exist. |
| github-readme-stats as hero | Stats are omitted. Public activity is modest; a hollow graph is worse than silence. |
| Emoji `## 🚀 About Me` | Plain markdown headings or none. Sigil is the ornament. |
| PerfectReadme-style component kit (banner, features, steps, install, dividers) | If the file tree looks like a product landing-page kit, delete files until it doesn’t. |
| GIFs as personality | Personality is the hook, the sigil, and the park-on-ACT. |
| “Craft” = animation count | Craft = custom lettering + one horizon that means something + theme-correct hairlines. |

**The test:** screenshot the README and blur the type. You should still recognize a datum and a basin, not a stack of capsules. If it reads as “nice widgets,” it failed.

---

## 6. Implementation notes for hand-authored SVG

### How to embed on GitHub
Use `<picture>` + `<img>`, not inline `<svg>` (GitHub sanitizes inline SVG hard: no SMIL reliability, CSS stripped). Official pattern:

```html
<picture>
 <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="assets/dist/hero-dark.svg">
 <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="assets/dist/hero-light.svg">
 <img src="assets/dist/hero-light.svg" width="880" alt="…full hook sentence…">
</picture>
```

Relative paths from the profile repo root work on `github.com/iamrishab`. Do not wrap in center tags. `width="880"` only; let height follow the viewBox.

**Alt:** hero = the hook verbatim. Act = the three beats + “AI that acts.” Work = the three metrics spoken as text. Stack = the five node names. Now = the current line. Identity and URLs also exist as real markdown.

### Fonts
- **Hook:** convert to outlines in the build (or in Figma/Illustrator before export). Outlines are the only way the serif italic is guaranteed inside SVG-as-`<img>`.
- **Do not** ship a full Newsreader file. A display face as base64 will bloat and still fail in some previewers.
- **`now` only:** subset IBM Plex Mono to `A–Z a–z 0–9 .,:;/+-–—&` and embed WOFF2 via `@font-face` in `<defs><style>`. License: OFL, keep the notice in `assets/fonts/NOTICE`.
- Hand-author labels in `act` / `stack` / `work` as outlines too, so those files have zero font dependency.

### SMIL vs CSS inside the SVG
Because these files are loaded as **images**, SMIL (`<animate>`, `<animateTransform>`, `<animateMotion>`) is the reliable motion path. CSS `@keyframes` inside the SVG *often* run in Chrome-as-img but are the first thing people confuse with “GitHub strips CSS” (that warning is about **inline** SVG in markdown, not `<img src="*.svg">`). **Author motion in SMIL.** Use CSS in the SVG only for static fills if useful — not for the living tick.

`stroke-dasharray` / `stroke-dashoffset` draw: set `pathLength="1"` so dash math is `0 → 1`, not a magic path length.

### Action pipeline (keep it small)
```
assets/src/tokens.json + assets/src/*.svg + now.yml
 ↓
 .github/workflows/svg.yml (on push; now.yml also weekly cron)
 ↓
 substitute tokens → hero-light/dark, act-*, work-*, stack-*, sigil-*
 text-to-path for any remaining <text> in static files
 inject now.yml string into now-light/dark (font subset already in file)
 ↓
 assets/dist/*
```

- **Do** use Actions as a **compiler** (one source, two themes, no drift).
- **Do** use Actions to refresh `now` from a hand-edited YAML — that is “alive” without scraping vanity stats.
- **Do not** use Actions to pull stars, streaks, trophies, visitor counts, or language pies.
- Commit `assets/dist` so the profile does not depend on a failed workflow to render.

Hand-author in a vector tool with a 880 grid, then clean IDs (`hook`, `horizon`, `basin`, `datum`, `tick`). No Illustrator cruft (`st0`, unused clip paths, `enable-background`).

### What GitHub will and will not do
- JS: dead. Hover: dead. External CSS: dead.
- SMIL in `<img>`: lives.
- `<picture>` theme switch: lives (GitHub blog, 2025).
- Filters: legal but heavy; a soft basin fill is enough — skip drop shadows and glow.
- Foreign objects / embedded HTML: treat as hostile; don’t.

### Proof before calling it done
1. Desktop light, desktop dark, mobile width (~360) light and dark — four screenshots of `github.com/iamrishab`.
2. Disable cache and confirm `<picture>` actually swaps (GitHub theme toggle, not only OS theme).
3. Read every essential word at 360px. If you have to pinch-zoom a label, it is decoration — delete it.
4. Select-all on the profile: name, role, links, and the hook (via alt + markdown) must exist as text.

---

## Copy, accessibility, brand (direction only — no README prose)

- **Voice stays in the hook and the park-on-ACT.** Body markdown should sound like the Immovable site’s honesty, not like a LinkedIn headline and not like a terminal demo.
- **Audience split:** work rows are founder metrics (money, latency, precision, “still up”). Stack is for peer engineers. Stats toys please neither.
- **a11y:** meaningful alt; real links in HTML; first frames complete; motion small; contrast ink-on-GitHub-bg (filament is accent, never body text).
- **Brand adjacency:** same seriousness as Immovable Tech, different object (instrument vs CLI). Do not reuse their `$` prompt or block cursor `▎`.

---

## Open questions for engineering (resolve before drawing)

1. **Three work metrics** — which numbers are public and founder-facing? (Resume has +50% CTR / 5k RPS, 28%→59% roof lines, 86% mIoU, 400M-MAU assistant, CES 2019. Pick three; do not invent Immovable portfolio figures on a personal profile unless they are his to claim.)
2. **Act words** — `SEE / CHOOSE / ACT` (mobile-safe) vs `OBSERVE / DECIDE / ACT` (clearer, tighter at 360px). Decide after a 360px print of the outlines.
3. **Display face** — Newsreader vs Source Serif 4. Both OFL-friendly enough if outlined (no runtime embed). Pick one italic that makes “feeling alive.” feel human, not editorial-template.
4. **`now` line** — worth a weekly Action, or a hand-edited SVG until the rest is shipped? Recommend: ship static `now` in v1, add the workflow only when the other four files are signed off.
5. **Certifications** — `<details>` or omit. They should not get an SVG plate.

Hand this to implementation as: **one sigil, one horizon, five files × two themes, plotter motion, transparent ground, stats and GIFs gone.** If a sixth SVG is proposed, the default answer is no.

A founder/CTO does not score seniority by widget density. They score **proof vs. decoration**. Your public graph is the opposite of a decoration surface.

| Streak + activity graph | You already ship these. If the graph is quiet, you are framing the quiet. |
| `lowlighter/metrics` Actions | A dashboard of zeros, rendered in SOTA chrome. |
| Typing SVG | “Building multi-agent systems…” rotating over 2019 TensorFlow OCR. That is a joke at your expense. |
| Trophy / visitor counter / follower badge | Internship energy. You already have Komarev views. Kill it. |
| Third-party Vercel/Heroku stats | 2021 junior default, plus an outage that replaces your profile with a broken image. |
| More GIFs on top of `hello.gif` + `neural.gif` | Same 2019 aesthetic, more of it. |
| Badge wall 2.0 (LangGraph, CrewAI, Bedrock AgentCore…) | Tools as identity, which you already named as the disease. |

**The taste failure:** “Maximal SOTA without looking like a generator” is a contradiction. Those artifacts *are* the generator. Self-hosting the same snake/typing/metrics does not make them original. It makes them a custom skin on a template everyone has seen.

**The audience failure:** Founders and CTOs do not hire from contribution heatmaps. Peer engineers who *do* look at GitHub will notice the heatmap first. Decorating it is how you lose both.

**The maintenance failure:** Actions that render SVGs on a schedule will fail. A senior profile that is sometimes a broken image is worse than a plain one. You also inherit foreign CSS, dark/light breakage, and GitHub mobile truncation. The first screen will be a banner, not a sentence.

If “SOTA” means anything here, it is **information architecture and one self-hosted visual**, not kit count.

---

## 2. Anonymizing employers: privacy theater that still doxes you

You cannot keep the **unique numbers** and lose the **names**. The names are not the leak. The fingerprints are.

| Claim you will be tempted to keep | Five-second Google |
|---|---|
| CES 2019 AI Conductor, autonomous golf cart, gesture + face | Yamaha press release. Your LinkedIn and dummy repo already attach your name. Anonymizing Yamaha is theater. |
| Conversational assistant for **400M MAU**, English + Hinglish | Airtel. Also internally inconsistent: 400M MAU vs “thousands of conversations a day.” |
| Aerial roof line detection, **28% → 59%**, 86% mIoU, US residential | EagleView. That metric pair is unique. |
| eCom search, **50% CTR**, **10% revenue**, **>5k RPS**, Milvus, Bangkok tenure | Makro. The site already launders this as “+50% CTR, +$12M/yr, 2,400 RPS” — the RPS does not even match. |
| “World’s first Privacy Enhanced Gateway,” +12% vs Google Vision on ICDAR 2013, −90% cost | FortressIQ / Automation Anywhere. “World’s first” is a press claim, not a README claim. |

Toptal details make this worse. If the implementer lifts them and strips logos, the fingerprints remain:

- NL2SQL + 5-layer SQL safeguards + Databricks → Aon
- MedPal, Emotion Code / Body Code, Zoho SalesIQ, FTC judges → Discover Healing
- 30k docs/day, 65% hallucination drop, 72% API cost cut → Invisible (and the homepage testimonial already says “30k docs a day”)
- MCP restaurant tools, 100% parity, “−56% MAPE” on the site → Mario Peng Lee
- Construction-site CCTV, 20h → 1h training → Latium
- Synthetic government polling → CGCN
- 3D-avatar therapist / neuroscientist RAG → Haadi / Revibe
- Pharma claim extraction, “>90%,” FDA framing → Solstice
- Dating-app LoRA + voice clone → Flirt

**Credibility vs privacy is a false binary.** The honest options are:

1. **Named, public, already-attributed work only** (CES is already public — but then you must not claim “sole owner of Yamaha’s CES booth”).
2. **Sector + constraint + failure mode, no unique metric.** “Telecom NLU, thousands of chats/day, Hinglish, production.” Not 400M.
3. **Proof lives on a call / under NDA.** GitHub states the class of problem, not the scoreboard.
4. **One current public artifact** from 2024–2026 that a stranger can clone. Without that, anonymized metrics are just ads.

**What will not work:** “Enterprise search, +50% CTR, 5k RPS, name withheld.” That is a press release with the letterhead torn off. A CTO either does not believe it, or reverse-searches it, or clicks LinkedIn and sees you were willing to name everyone *there*. The split (LinkedIn names names, GitHub plays spy) looks like you are hiding, not protecting clients.

**Immovable Tech as the only named entity is the highest-risk name you can print.** LinkedIn company page: 1 person, founded 2025. About page: “we don’t have any juniors,” 12+ years average tenure, 3 continents on-call. Homepage: Fortune 1000, React 19 / Apple Intelligence / ARCore, case studies (fraud +$47M, IoT +$8.6M, BLE payments, AR training) that do **not** appear on the resume, plus testimonials that recycle resume/Toptal numbers. Counters show 0+. If the README’s proof surface is “Founder, Immovable Tech → immovabletech.com,” you are sending a skeptical buyer to a site that currently argues with your CV.

Also: the site already says “0 NDAs broken.” Publishing client metrics on GitHub is how you make that line look like copy.

---

## 3. Claims that are risky, unverifiable, or inflated

**Title and time (will be checked)**

- 8 vs 8+ vs 9 years. Career start Jan 2018 → Sep 2026 is ~8.7. “9” is a round-up. “8 years of chatbots” and “6 years of LLMs” on Toptal are category inflation.
- Founder & Head of AI vs Head of AI vs Staff ML Developer vs “AI / Platform Engineering Architect.”
- Immovable start: Jun 2024 / Jul 2024 / 2025. Company founded 2025 vs work in 2024.
- “2 years 4 months” on LinkedIn vs the calendar.
- DeepSeek “2 years,” Flux as a top skill, Voiceflow as expertise: trend tags, not identity.

**Numbers that will not survive “show me the eval”**

- **400M MAU.** You did not serve 400M users. You worked on a surface inside a company that reports that MAU. Keep this and you look like every inflated India-IT resume a CTO has already discarded.
- **85% accuracy** on that assistant. Accuracy of what? Intent? Containment? CSAT? Without a definition it is noise.
- **50% CTR, 10% incremental revenue, 5k RPS.** Ownership, window, incrementality, and whether search or ads drove revenue. The site already retells this with different RPS and a dollar figure. Three versions = zero versions.
- **28% → 59% “accuracy” on line detection.** Line detection is not usually reported as accuracy. A vision lead will ask “precision/recall at what IoU, what split, what obstruction rate?” 86% mIoU@0.5 is the only number here that sounds like a real paper metric — and it still fingerprints EagleView.
- **−25% latency, −30% VRAM, INT8 QAT.** Plausible. Still need baseline model, batch, GPU, and whether you owned Triton in prod.
- **−40% operational overhead** (Immovable). Undefined. Overhead of whose ops?
- **Sub-second RAG on complex enterprise data.** Everyone’s README. Latency without corpus size, hop count, and failure rate is marketing.
- **World’s first PEG. +12% vs Google Vision on ICDAR 2013. −90% infra cost.** ICDAR vs a cloud API is often a mismatched eval. “World’s first” and “−90%” are extraordinary.
- **5.35% quarterly sales** from ARIMA as a GET. Attribution on retail sales to a junior forecasting project is the first number a skeptical reader drops.
- Toptal-only: **65% / 30k/day / 92% / 72% / 100% parity / 56% / 40% / 35% / 95% train-time / >90% claims.** None of these are on the resume you called the source of truth. Several already leaked onto the company site. Treat them as **banned until you can defend the eval in a call without naming the client.**

**Work that is true and still wrong to feature**

- Energy-healing RAG (Emotion Code / Body Code) and “FTC policy judges.”
- 3D-avatar therapist / “neuroscientist emulation” / CBT-DBT tone.
- Dating-app voice clone + LoRA “SOTA.”
- Synthetic government polling / “proprietary LLM on mass poll data” for a POC.

A founder hiring an AI studio will not think “versatile.” They will think “you will put my brand next to woo, dating, and political synth.”

**Current README lies the plan must not replace with prettier lies**

- AWS ML Specialty, GCP Professional ML Engineer, Azure AI Engineer, NVIDIA DLI — **not on resume or LinkedIn.** LinkedIn certs are OpenCV Udemy-tier. If you cannot link a credly/acclaim URL, it is a fabrication. Delete the section. Do not “SOTA-ify” it.

**Public proof that is weak if you spotlight it**

- Stack Overflow **1633**. The current SO widget is a self-own. Do not rebuild it.
- CES: Yamaha exhibited PPM + AI Conductor as a **corporate** booth. “Solely owned and showcased at CES” from a first-job engineer will be discounted. The public repo is a dummy. You can say you shipped gesture/face/tracking into a CES demo. You cannot say you were CES.

---

## 4. Refuse even if every kit includes it

**Visual / infra**

- Visitor counters, streak, trophy, snake, 3D contrib, metrics dashboards, activity graphs, “profile views,” follower pills
- `readme-typing-svg` and rotating title lists
- Third-party stats hosts (Vercel/Heroku/komarev)
- Badge walls, skill bars, “tech stack as identity”
- Centered emoji H2s (`🚀 About Me`, `🧰 Tech Stack`, `💬 Ask me about`)
- Wave headers, neural GIFs, more hero animation than one static idea
- Spotify, WakaTime, chess, “latest blog” when `blog` is empty
- “Available for hire” banners that fight the studio pitch
- Toptal badge, “Verified Expert,” marketplace skill comma-lists
- Phone number from the resume
- Any Action whose failure blanked the profile

**Content**

- Unverified cloud/NVIDIA certs; Udemy certs
- Client names, Toptal, and unique metrics that invert to a client
- “World’s first,” “SOTA outcomes,” “cutting-edge,” “enterprise-grade,” “self-orchestrating”
- 400M MAU, world’s first PEG, therapist-mimic, energy healing, voice-clone dating, political synth
- Immovable site case studies that are not on the resume (fraud +$47M, IoT +$8.6M, BLE, AR)
- Fake or laundered testimonials
- Tool catalogs (CrewAI, AutoGen, Bedrock AgentCore, Voiceflow, DeepSeek-as-identity)
- “Ask me about,” “passionate developer,” “I don’t just assist — I act”
- Studio “we” copied from a 1-person LinkedIn company
- A second resume. LinkedIn already exists.

If the implementer needs a rule: **if a bootcamp README has it, it is out.**

---

## 5. Voice risks

You already have three incompatible voices. A “ghostwritten original” pass will puree them.

1. **The bio (keep, or do not touch).** “My loss function in life is feeling alive” is the only sentence on the profile that does not sound generated. Replacing it with LinkedIn’s “Building AI that acts, not just answers” is how you kill the only human signal you have.
2. **LinkedIn summary.** Em dashes, “I have consistently delivered,” “well-architected, long-running platforms,” “systems that don’t just assist — they act.” That is ChatGPT cadence. Do not import it.
3. **Toptal.** “Don’t just work in theory; they ship.” Verified-expert English. CTOs who have hired off Toptal will recognize the scrape.
4. **Immovable site.** Literary agency: incident channels, Friday-afternoon systems, “written in Python, read over coffee,” ten things we’ll lose a contract over. Competent, and already slightly too written. If GitHub sounds like the same ghostwriter, the two tabs confirm each other as marketing.
5. **Resume bullets.** Metric stacking. Fine on a CV. On GitHub, without names, it reads as unverifiable brag.

**Specific tics to ban**

- Rule of three; “I don’t X. I Y.”
- “Partner with founders/CEOs/CTOs to unlock / 0-to-1 / production-grade”
- “Cutting-edge” (LinkedIn Immovable uses it three times)
- “Staff / Architect / Head of” stacking in one paragraph
- “We” when LinkedIn says one employee
- Parallel clauses with em dashes
- Humor that explains itself; ML metaphors beyond the existing bio

Ghostwriting will fail in the usual way: it will sound *more* written than you, and more like the site. The target is a short, specific, slightly dry first person — or a clearly labeled studio page that does not pretend to be a 40-person bench.

---

## 6. Better alternatives the plan is likely to miss

These beat any widget list.

1. **Fix the GitHub profile chrome first.** Set company, website (`immovabletech.com` only after the 0+ counters and invented case studies are cleaned), location, and pins. Empty metadata plus a maximal README is costume.
2. **Pin three honest repos, rewrite those READMEs, archive the fork pile.** The profile README cannot outrun 88 dusty forks. `DB-tf` as a pin says 2019. A CTO who clicks pins will not come back to your prose.
3. **One current public artifact from 2024–2026.** NL2SQL safeguards, LTR/search eval, Triton/INT8 notes, RAG failure modes — **without** client fingerprints. That is the actual senior signal. The dummy CES repo does not count.
4. **Twelve to twenty lines, not a landing-page kit.** Thesis. Three problem classes (search/ranking, vision-on-the-edge, agents-with-eval). One CTA: LinkedIn for named history, email/`immovabletech.com` for work. Stop.
5. **If you need a visual: one self-hosted SVG, no third-party render.** No animation that implies a busy graph. Dark and light. If it needs an Action, it is too fragile.
6. **Do not show the contribution graph.** Hiding a quiet graph is stronger than decorating it.
7. **Constraint cards, not scoreboards.** “Aerial lines, obstruction, Triton budget.” “Catalog search, tail queries, ranking vs revenue.” “NL2SQL, warehouse, read-only, retries.” No 50%, no 400M, no 5k RPS.
8. **Decide the product.** Hiring **you** and hiring **a studio** are different pages. Right now resume = founder, LinkedIn = Head of AI at a 1-person shop, site = agency bench. Pick one. The README cannot fix a three-way identity split.
9. **Put proof on Immovable, then link it — after the site is true.** Do not clone the about page onto GitHub. Do not invent a fourth scoreboard.
10. **Stack Overflow: a text link, or nothing.** No widget.
11. **Delete certs and the visitor counter in the first edit.** That is the highest-ROI change and requires no research.

---

## 7. Hard questions the implementer must get right

If any of these are fudged, do not write the README yet.

1. **After 20 seconds, what does the CTO do?** Email, book a call, click LinkedIn, click the site, or bounce? Design for one action.
2. **I or we?** Reconcile 1 LinkedIn employee, “Founder,” “Head of AI,” and “140 years / no juniors.” The README cannot invent a pod the company page does not have.
3. **Which three claims survive “show me the eval, the split, and who else touched it” without breaking an NDA?** If you cannot name three, you do not have a README; you have a wish.
4. **Will unique metrics stay if they deanonymize the client?** If yes, drop the anonymity rule. If no, drop the metrics. Not both.
5. **CES: drop, or accept it is Yamaha?** There is no third path.
6. **8 or 9 years? Founder or Head of AI? 2024 or 2025?** Pick the most conservative number that all three documents can survive.
7. **Is there one 2024–2026 public artifact you will actually publish?** If no, stop promising “proof.”
8. **Energy healing, therapist-mimic, voice-clone dating, political synth: on-profile or buried?** Default: buried.
9. **Source of truth when resume, LinkedIn, Toptal, and the site disagree?** Toptal is a lead magnet, not a fact database. The site’s case studies are not importable until they match work you will defend.
10. **Are you selling a studio or selling yourself?** “Available for hire” + Founder + agency “we” is three CTAs.
11. **Will you link `immovabletech.com` while it shows 0+ and case studies that are not on the CV?** If yes, you are asking GitHub to inherit the site’s credibility hole.
12. **Keep the bio?** If you “professionalize” it, you will sound like everyone else.
13. **What is the rollback if an Action or third-party SVG dies?** If the answer is “the profile looks broken,” do not add the Action.
14. **What must a peer engineer believe that a founder does not need?** If the answer is “I am current, not a 2019 CV repo guy,” then pins and one new repo matter more than prose.
15. **Phone number, Toptal, certs, visitor count: confirm they are hard-deleted.** Not restyled.

---

## What I would force into the plan as constraints

- **No third-party widgets. No contribution visualizations. No badge walls. No certs. No visitor counter.**
- **No client names, no Toptal, no unique reverse-searchable metrics.**
- **No site case studies that are absent from the resume.**
- **No “we” unless the company page and the about page are made consistent with a 1-person (or honestly described) studio.**
- **Source-of-truth pass before a single sentence is drafted.** Conservative tenure, one title, one start date.
- **Visual budget: at most one self-hosted graphic. Prefer zero until the pins and metadata are fixed.**
- **Success test:** a CTO who does not know you can explain what you do in one sentence, is not embarrassed by the graph, and has one place to go next. If the README needs a snake to feel finished, it is not finished.

The work is not to look like the best README in the world. The work is to stop looking like a generator, stop publishing numbers you cannot defend, and stop asking animation to cover a quiet public GitHub. That is a writing and honesty problem. Kits will not solve it.
</response>

Embedding subset WOFF2 is too complex. The now line will be outlined with fontTools instead. Fonts will live in assets/fonts/ with an OFL NOTICE. compile_svgs.py will generate all static SVGs. render_now.py will update now-light and now-dark from now.yml using the same pipeline. SVG geometries are being designed now. The sigil will be 48 by 48 pixels.

The sigil geometry is now defined. It features a circle basin, a crosshair, a loss curve, and an animated filament dot.

The hero layout is planned at 880 by 320 pixels. Three left-aligned Newsreader lines will sit above a descending horizon curve. The sigil will anchor near the last word. Tick marks and a filament dot will mark the bottom.

The act section is 880 by 88 pixels. It will display SEE, CHOOSE, and ACT across a polyline.

The token will travel along a hairline path and park on ACT for 40 percent of the 14-second loop. KeyPoints and keyTimes will be set so the motion begins already sitting on ACT, with the token spending 60 percent of the cycle moving and 40 percent resting.

The planned keyPoints and keyTimes values were too messy. Placing the token statically on ACT and animating from there was considered, but jumping back to SEE would look broken. A loop that holds on ACT for 40 percent of the cycle while traveling the full path remains unresolved.

The act animation will use a five-point keyPoints sequence: 1, 1, 0, 0.5, 1. Corresponding keyTimes will be 0, 0.4, 0.41, 0.7, and 1. This keeps the token on ACT for the first 40 percent of the loop, then moves it across the path to ACT over the remaining 60 percent.

A jump from ACT back to SEE at 0.4–0.41 seconds is accepted as a cheap way to hold the token on ACT for the first 40 percent of the loop. The alternative of reversing the path continuously was rejected. The square will be placed at ACT by default, then animateMotion will travel it across the path to ACT over the remaining 60 percent.

The act animation keyPoints and keyTimes are finalized. The token will hold on ACT for the first 40 percent of the loop, then travel across the path to ACT over the remaining 60 percent.

The work section will be 880 by 260 pixels. Three rows will sit at y=50, 130, and 210. The metrics will be large and outlined, using a mono or serif typeface.

The stack section will be 880 by 168 pixels. Five labeled circles will sit on a spine. A filament tick will walk the spine for sixteen seconds.

The now section will be 880 by 52 pixels. A sixteen-pixel sigil will sit beside the word NOW. The line will come from the YAML file.

Static TTFs will be downloaded from Google Fonts to simplify fontTools outlining. The Python compiler will use uv with fonttools, pyyaml, ruff, and mypy. Every line will be thoroughly commented.

render_now.py will read now.yml and fail closed if the file is empty, preventing accidental overwrites. Shared SVG helpers will move into a dedicated module rather than staying inside the render script. All imports will be grouped at the top of every file, and every parameter will be used. The work section heading will be a single markdown word as specified.

Headings will be plain markdown labels such as `## Work` and `## Stack`, with no emojis. The retail lifecycle will be omitted as optional, keeping the document lean.

The compiler will generate src templates containing tokens for the geometric sections. Outlined text will be drawn by instantiating variable fonts, extracting glyphs, and converting them to SVG paths with fontTools pens. The pyproject.toml will require Python 3.12 or higher.

Only the three required font files will be downloaded to keep the repository lightweight. A local HTML preview will be created for browser verification, since pushing to live GitHub is not yet possible.

```bash
python3 << 'PY'
from pathlib import Path
root = Path("/Users/rishabpal/Projects/personal/iamrishab")
readme = (root / "README.md").read_text()
# Expand picture tags to both themes side by side for review
html = f"""<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>Profile README preview</title>
<style>
  body {{ margin: 0; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; }}
  .wrap {{ display: flex; }}
  .col {{ flex: 1; padding: 32px 40px 80px; box-sizing: border-box; }}
  .light {{ background: #ffffff; color: #1f2328; }}
  .dark {{ background: #0d1117; color: #e6edf3; }}
  .col img {{ display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 880px; height: auto; }}
  .col a {{ color: inherit; }}
  .narrow {{ max-width: 390px; margin: 40px auto; border: 1px solid #d0d7de; }}
  h1,h2 {{ font-weight: 600; }}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <div class="col light" id="light"></div>
  <div class="col dark" id="dark"></div>
</div>
<div class="narrow light" id="narrow"></div>
<script>
const md = {readme!r};
function render(theme) {{
  let html = md
    .replace(/<picture>[\\s\\S]*?<img src="([^"]+)"([^>]*)>/g, (m, src, rest) => {{
      const themed = src.replace('-light.svg', '-' + theme + '.svg');
      return '<img src="' + themed + '"' + rest + '>';
    }})
    .replace(/<\\/picture>/g, '')
    .replace(/^## (.+)$/gm, '<h2>$1</h2>')
    .replace(/\\[([^\\]]+)\\]\\(([^)]+)\\)/g, '<a href="$2">$1</a>')
    .replace(/\\*\\*([^*]+)\\*\\*/g, '<strong>$1</strong>')
    .replace(/<details>[\\s\\S]*?<\\/details>/g, '')
    .replace(/\\n\\n/g, '</p><p>')
    .replace(/^(\\d+)\\. /gm, '<br>$1. ');
  return '<p>' + html + '</p>';
}}
document.getElementById('light').innerHTML = render('light');
document.getElementById('dark').innerHTML = render('dark');
document.getElementById('narrow').innerHTML = '<p>390px</p>' + render('light');
</script>
</body>
</html>
"""
out = Path("/tmp/iamrishab-preview.html")
# Use file paths that work from file://
html = html.replace('src="assets/', f'src="{root}/assets/')
out.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")
print(out)
PY
ls -la /tmp/iamrishab-preview.html
```

```bash
uv run python - << 'PY'
from scripts.datum import outline_text, plex_mono, newsreader
mono = plex_mono()
italic = newsreader(italic=True)
regular = newsreader(italic=False)
for label, font, size, text in [
    ("hook1", regular, 46, "My loss function"),
    ("hook2", regular, 46, "in life is"),
    ("hook3", italic, 52, "feeling alive."),
    ("now", mono, 18, "NOW shipping multi-agent systems with evals and a paper trail"),
    ("nowline", mono, 18, "shipping multi-agent systems with evals and a paper trail"),
    ("catalog", mono, 20, "catalog search"),
    ("metric2", mono, 38, "28% -> 59%"),
    ("metric2u", mono, 38, "28% → 59%"),
]:
    d, w = outline_text(font, text, size, 0, 0)
    print(f"{label:10} {w:7.1f}  path={len(d)}")
PY
```
